chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him, 'When a woman dies, who is most entitled among people to pray over her?' He said, 'Her husband.' I said, 'Is the husband more entitled than the father, the son, and the brother?' He said, 'Yes, and he washes her.'

key_terms.يُغَسِّلُهَا: He washes her (referring to ritual washing of the body)

ai.seo_question: Who has the primary right to pray over a deceased woman according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juridical hierarchy for the funeral prayer of a woman, establishing the husband as the primary incumbent (ahaq) even over male agnates like the father and son, while also linking this right to the duty of washing the body (ghusl). This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly view that the husband’s marital bond grants him precedence in ritual duties, distinguishing it from inheritance shares. The narration underscores the practical integration of ritual purification and communal prayer within the family structure.
